_comment: Phase 6.3 (edge security) — the AWS WAFv2 equivalent of
cloudflare-waf-ruleset.tf, provider-portable per this step's own brief.
This is the `Rules` array of a `AWS::WAFv2::WebACL` (CloudFormation) /
aws wafv2 create-web-acl (CLI/SDK) request, scoped REGIONAL (attach to
the ALB/API Gateway in front of deploy/k8s/'s own ingress) or
CLOUDFRONT (attach to the CDN distribution — see ../cdn/README.md).
NOT applied anywhere: no AWS account/ALB exists in this environment.
Validate with `aws wafv2 check-capacity` and a real `put-web-acl` dry
run against your own account before relying on this.
See README.md in this directory for the full rule catalog and the
edge-vs-app rate-limit interaction this rule set is one half of.
Name: hrm-web-acl

Rules.Name: AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet
Rules._overrideActionNote: COUNT (log-only) for the first deploy window — see README.md's 'roll out WAF rules in LOG mode first' note. Switch to `{}` (i.e. no override — let the managed group's own Block actions apply) once a real traffic sample has been reviewed.

Rules.Name: AWS-AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet
Rules._note: Covers path-traversal-shaped and other known-bad-input signatures — the managed equivalent of cloudflare-waf-ruleset.tf's hand-written path-traversal custom rule.

Rules.Name: hrm-block-scanner-user-agents
Rules._note: AWS Managed Rules' Bot Control group is a real option here but is a separately-billed add-on this codebase's own docs deliberately don't assume is purchased — see README.md. This custom rule is the always-available fallback: block known scanner/exploit-tool User-Agents outright, the same list cloudflare-waf-ruleset.tf uses.

Rules.Name: hrm-request-size-limit
Rules._note: Matches deploy/k8s/base/ingress.yaml's own nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size: '10m' AND careers.controller.ts's MAX_RESUME_SIZE_BYTES (10MB) — never set lower than either, or a legitimate resume upload gets rejected at the edge before it ever reaches the app's own already-correct limit.

Rules.Name: hrm-ip-rate-limit
Rules._note: The COARSE, IP-based volumetric layer — see README.md's 'edge vs app rate limiting' section. AWS WAFv2 rate-based rules count over a trailing 5-minute window natively; 2000/5min per source IP is deliberately generous and NOT tenant-aware — TenantRateLimitService (0.10) remains the precise, per-tenant/per-edition control at the app layer.
